donors.reason: BET bromodomain inhibitor like JQ1-S; supports shared BRD4 inhibition mechanism affecting histone acetylation and downstream methylation.
DOT1L inhibitor directly reduces H3K79 methylation, matching H3K79me0 increase and H3K79me1 decrease.

revised_hypotheses: JQ1-S inhibits BRD4, displacing it from acetylated chromatin and reducing H3K9ac/H3K14ac, which may indirectly lower H3K79 methylation and increase H3K79me0.
JQ1-S may indirectly inhibit DOT1L via BRD4-dependent transcription, reducing H3K79me1 and increasing H3K79me0, similar to EPZ-5676.
The observed H3K56me0 increase may reflect BRD4-dependent regulation of histone modifiers, but no donor evidence directly supports this link.
Donor compounds with high anchor similarity (decitabine, zebularine, methylstat) lack retrieved pharmacological descriptions relevant to these histone marks, so their support is unsupported.
unresolved: No retrieved source describes methylstat, decitabine, or zebularine effects on the queried histone marks; their anchor similarity alone is insufficient.
No direct evidence links JQ1-S to H3K56me0, H3K27me0K36me2, or H3K9me0K14ac1 changes in A375 cells.
The causal chain from BRD4 inhibition to H3K79 methylation changes remains hypothetical without transcriptomic or enzymatic data.
